macro_context.market_sentiment: Risk-on as of May 6, 2026. S&P 500 +0.72%, Dow +0.94%, Nasdaq +0.73%, Russell 2000 +1.75%, driven by U.S.-Iran de-escalation hopes and a strong earnings season (AMD beat, Nvidia-Corning deal). Ceasefire optimism reversed the May 4 sell-off triggered by UAE missile interception.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 — the most dissent-laden FOMC vote since 1992 (4 dissents). Markets pricing zero rate moves in 2026 and only one 25bp cut in December 2027. Powell stepped down as chair but remains on the board; leadership transition adds uncertainty.
macro_context.geopolitical: U.S.-Iran military conflict is the dominant risk: oil prices spiked on May 4 after UAE intercepted Iranian missiles, then fell May 5-6 on ceasefire framework hopes. Background risks include U.S. tariffs/trade policy, NATO posture near Greenland, and Venezuela civil unrest. Elevated energy prices are feeding inflation.

web_context.competitor_activity: Google Cloud posted the fastest growth (+63% YoY) among the three hyperscalers in Q1 2026, outpacing Azure and AWS. Key competitive development: OpenAI is aggressively shifting its primary cloud relationship from Microsoft to Amazon (AWS), launching GPT-5.5 on Amazon Bedrock — this weakens Microsoft's AI moat and marginally benefits AWS over Google, but the departure of OpenAI from Microsoft reduces pressure on Google Search in some enterprise segments. All three hyperscalers beat AI-driven cloud demand estimates, confirming broad sector tailwinds. Sources: CNBC (April 30, 2026), Axios, AWS News Blog.
